1: //! Implementation of `LazyKey` for Windows.
2: //!
3: //! Windows has no native support for running destructors so we manage our own
4: //! list of destructors to keep track of how to destroy keys. We then install a
5: //! callback later to get invoked whenever a thread exits, running all
6: //! appropriate destructors (see the [`guard`](guard) module documentation).
7: //!
8: //! This will likely need to be improved over time, but this module attempts a
9: //! "poor man's" destructor callback system. Once we've got a list of what to
10: //! run, we iterate over all keys, check their values, and then run destructors
11: //! if the values turn out to be non null (setting them to null just beforehand).
12: //! We do this a few times in a loop to basically match Unix semantics. If we
13: //! don't reach a fixed point after a short while then we just inevitably leak
14: //! something.
15: //!
16: //! The list is implemented as an atomic single-linked list of `LazyKey`s and
17: //! does not support unregistration. Unfortunately, this means that we cannot
18: //! use racy initialization for creating the keys in `LazyKey`, as that could
19: //! result in destructors being missed. Hence, we synchronize the creation of
20: //! keys with destructors through [`INIT_ONCE`](c::INIT_ONCE) (`std`'s
21: //! [`Once`](crate::sync::Once) cannot be used since it might use TLS itself).
22: //! For keys without destructors, racy initialization suffices.

113:         if is_thread_local_initializer(cx, fn_kind, span).unwrap_or(false)
114:             // Some implementations of `thread_local!` include an initializer fn.
115:             // In the case of a const initializer, the init fn is also const,
116:             // so we can skip the lint in that case. This occurs only on some

cause.fact: All five project initializers already use explicit const blocks. No user initializer is missing const.
cause.targetFact: Fixed nightly --print cfg includes target_thread_local for i686-pc-windows-msvc and i686-win7-windows-gnu, but not i686-win7-windows-msvc. Vendor alone is insufficient to scope a workaround.
cause.macroFact: std/sys/thread_local/mod.rs dispatches the non-native target to os.rs. Its sole @key $init:expr arm also matches const blocks and emits an ordinary fn __rust_std_internal_init_fn. thread/local.rs forwards user const correctly; the OS fallback does not preserve a const-fn distinction.
cause.lintFact: Pinned Clippy check_fn recognizes thread_local-generated item functions and skips only tcx.is_const_fn(defid). It then const-qualifies MIR without detecting that the original return is already an inline const. Thus the ordinary generated OS initializer is reported. The source comment assumes constant initializers generate constant functions, which is false for this pinned fallback.
cause.classification: Generated OS-backend false positive supported by actual CI diagnostics plus exact pinned source; this investigation did not execute a new isolated repro.

minimalRecommendation.strategy: Keep every thread_local declaration, explicit const block, initializer value/type and destructor test unchanged. After exact-target isolated repro confirms placement, apply an individually reasoned cfg_attr(expect) inside thread_local immediately before each of the five affected static declarations. No crate/module/global allow or lint-group weakening.

minimalRecommendation.condition: clippy AND target_os=windows AND target_vendor=win7 AND target_env=msvc; do not apply to Win7 GNU or modern MSVC because their pinned native backends do not emit this false positive.
minimalRecommendation.whyExpect: An upstream fix that stops the warning must produce unfulfilled_lint_expectations under -D warnings, forcing removal of the workaround instead of silently keeping an allow.
minimalRecommendation.scopeLimit: This is a narrowly documented compiler-generated false positive, not permission to suppress a real missing-const initializer elsewhere. No toolchain/std macro patch is proposed.

minimalReproProposal.suggestedComparison: Use exact nightly and build-std with the existing i686-win7-windows-msvc target to Clippy-check this dependency-free lib, first unchanged to reproduce 2 diagnostics; then with per-static conditional expect to get no diagnostics. Compare modern MSVC and Win7 GNU unchanged with strict -D warnings. Do not claim host-native results reproduce the Win7 OS fallback.
minimalReproProposal.acceptance: Retain normal strict -D warnings. Confirm exact original five source declarations and existing real held-TLS-destructor tests still compile/run on Windows; do not remove/drop/shorten their held ownership assertions.

dropGuarantees.preserve: The same std LocalKey/Storage remains responsible for thread-local values. OS fallback Storage::new registers destroy_value; Windows LazyKey keeps its destructor list and Windows guard arranges cleanup. Attribute-only change does not change initialization, storage, lifetime, registration or Drop execution.
